limits: No alternative implementation or benchmark executed; no language or scheduler performance ranking.
No network identity, execution authority, physical, hard-real-time, MLS/CNSA, availability or whole-lane qualification.
component: Process-local inbox quota, expiry, clock-fault and close accounting
constraints: Synchronous producers/consumers; at most sixteen exact immutable payloads, 65536 bytes each and 1 MiB retained total, plus per-peer count bound. Reject incoming saturation without dropping older live entries.
Caller-monotonic safe-integer time, all-entry exclusive expiry, permanent close on clock fault. Explicit close clears queued references only; lock acquisition may block.
No transport or idle purge timer; no hard completion-time, fairness, RSS or shutdown-latency bound.
alternatives: Python deque and one explicit lock for combined quota/expiry updates.
Rust crossbeam bounded channels plus a synchronized byte/peer/expiry ledger.
C#/F# bounded channels with explicit full behavior plus combined accounting.
Erlang/Elixir queue operations in a serialized process; filter can implement full-queue expiry, with explicit admission/backlog control.
rationale: KEEP after twelve current methods including supervised concurrency, distinct admitted bytes, expiry behind a live head, clock faults and close limitations. No new mismatch found.

Count-bounded channels alone do not enforce aggregate bytes, peer quotas or expiry. Current single critical section covers all those predicates at fixed small count; immutable payloads retain identity without asynchronous staging.

OTP offers immutable queue/filter operations; a managed process adds a separate message-admission boundary. Native channels are credible for future native deployment, but no measured contention or target requirement establishes a material advantage here.
Changing exclusive expiry to inclusive expiry causes an existing assertion failure. This confirms selected test sensitivity, not a formal concurrency or hard-time proof.
